this might be the best week in tech so far this year. Fable 5 got extended until July 17th. OpenAI also released the GPT-5.6 family. both are amazing on their own. together, they’re one of the greatest tools a builder can have right now. Fable 5 is still the best model I’ve used for architecture, planning, understanding tradeoffs, and figuring out how a large task should actually be approached. the issue is the usage limits. even on Anthropic’s 20x Max plan, it’s extremely easy to burn through your subscription. so I built a setup that lets Fable stay in charge while delegating most of the work to the GPT-5.6 family. here’s how I use them: -> Sol is OpenAI’s strongest reasoning model. great for long tasks and complex implementation. it will get it done. -> Terra is a solid middle-ground worker. good for tasks that need more than a basic model without using Sol. -> Luna is dirt cheap and ideal for simple work like searching files, gathering context, or small tasks. Fable handles the architecture, planning, delegation, and final review. the GPT-5.6 models handle the execution. Fable can even delegate tasks that use OpenAI’s computer-use capabilities, which is still by far the best way I’ve found to give an agent real access to your computer. this means it can gather context, refactor large sections of a codebase, investigate issues, implement changes, test the work, and send agents back in when something is still broken. a task that would previously burn through my weekly Fable usage within 30 minutes now uses around 5% of my 5 hour limit. Fable gets to focus on what it’s best at instead of wasting its limited usage on every small implementation step. the GPT-5.6 models get a much smarter system planning and reviewing their work. I’ve been using this for long coding tasks, large refactors, parallel issue fixing, context gathering, and everything in between. comment “foreman” and I’ll send you the repo. #buildinpublic #ai #codex #claudecode #codingagents

got invited to a dinner with 20 of the most ambitious founders in sf. walked in expecting good conversations. walked out with a completely different level of clarity. everyone at the table was building, selling, scaling, or figuring out distribution at an insane level. huge thanks to Pavan Kumar for the invite and to the Clean team for putting this together. also grateful to Kevin Yu from Llama Ventures for co-hosting. this summer i’ve been heads down on RocketRide . the biggest pain i keep seeing with AI teams is that the stack changes every week. new model. new provider. new agent framework. new tool standard. new “best practice.” and every time the ecosystem shifts, teams end up rebuilding pieces of their workflow again. RocketRide is the AI infrastructure layer that outlasts those changes. build your AI agents/pipelines once. swap models, tools, providers, and services without rewriting everything. run it locally, self-hosted, or in the cloud. trace what happens across every node. move fast without locking yourself into whatever the current hype cycle says is best. basically, a meta-harness for AI teams building production workflows that need to survive past the next version upgrade. SF has made one thing extremely obvious to me: the builders who win are are building systems that keep working when everything around them changes. more soon. #buildinpublic #ai #startups #gtm #studentswhobuild #rocketride

a forecast I read is the reason I'm in SF right now A few summers ago I was messing around on Replit, watching random AI videos, and stumbled across a deep dive on AI 2027. read it and couldn't stop. it showed me we're in the middle of one of the biggest technological shifts in history, and that's what sent me down the path that eventually landed me in SF. Seeing GPT-5.6 move through a limited rollout at the government's request, and Fable/Mythos access get suspended after national-security concerns reminded me of AI 2027 (a forecast about frontier AI, arms races, and loss of control). a lot of people are framing this as government overreach or labs losing momentum. I understand that concern, but I don't think that's the only way to see it. AI 2027 is essentially about what happens when every lab and every government races forward because standing still feels like losing. building blindly. shipping fast. treating caution as weakness. what we're seeing now, phased releases, safety evaluations, more outside review before broad public access, might be the start of something healthier. I'm not saying blanket bans or permanent gatekeeping are the answer. but given how uncertain things are at the frontier, slowing down slightly and being more deliberate seems reasonable. I'm curious if this turns into something consistent and transparent with real standards, or if it stays reactive. one is progress. other is politics dressed up as safety. Link in the comments. Check out AI 2027 if you haven't, genuinely one of the most important things I've come across.

What if you could give Claude your memories? Well now you might be able to... Introducing Timeslicer MCP Timeslicer is a desktop app that shows you how you use your time. Our calendar view is visually interesting, but lacked insight. Now, you can simply talk to claude or any agent about your time: - "What was that one claude chat link?" - "How much time did I spent on linkedin?" - "How much progress was made on the new auth feature I assigned?" We also launched teams mode, letting you invite colleagues and gain time observability company-wide. We are currently running a limited enterprise beta so shoot me a DM!

I’ve never been particularly good at staying in one lane. Over the past several years, some of my most formative experiences have taken place in very different environments - from investment research and manufacturing floors to building small businesses, studying abroad, exploring the outdoors, or developing my own watch company. Until now, I haven't shared much of that journey here. As I enter another year at Chapman University studying Finance alongside Art History & the Chapman Honors Program, I want to use this page more intentionally - not only to share what I'm working on now, but also to reflect on some of the experiences that have shaped how I think about business, investing, leadership, and the kind of career I want to build. A common thread has emerged across seemingly unrelated experiences: I'm most interested in understanding how value is created, identified, and communicated - whether that's in a company, an investment, a physical product, or a work of art. Over the next few weeks, I'll be looking back at some of those experiences while sharing what I'm working toward next. There’s a lot still to figure out. That's part of what makes it exciting.

MCP V2 landed, and it flips the whole model: MCP is stateless now. 🚀 No initialize handshake, no session IDs. Every request carries its own version, identity, and capabilities, so your server runs behind a plain load balancer with no sticky sessions. Our AI engineer, Joshua Phillips breaks down everything that changed on the streets of San Francisco in under a minute. Watch, then tell us: simpler or just different? #MCP #AIEngineering #AIInfrastructure #AgenticAI #RocketRideCloud

Earlier this month, I had the privilege of presenting our poster, “GrapeSense: Automated Grape-Leaf Disease Detection Using a Deep Learning Pipeline on Augmented Vineyard Imagery,” at the IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC) in Golden, Colorado. Our two-stage deep learning system uses YOLOv8 to detect grape leaves from drone imagery and ResNet-18 to classify each as healthy or diseased, achieving 93% detection accuracy and 99.6% classification accuracy. Seeing our model translate from a research idea to a tool that could help real vineyards combat crop loss was incredibly inspiring. I’m also thrilled to share that our work has been accepted for publication and presentation at the upcoming IEEE SmartAgri&Susy 2025: Where Technology Meets Sustainable Agriculture conference! As a high school senior, I joined the GrapeSense project, having no idea that it would shape how I see the intersection of machine learning and real-world impact. What began as an exploration of computer vision for agriculture became a multi-institution research effort demonstrating how technology can empower sustainability. Getting to contribute to this project so early on showed me how machine learning truly transcends fields, from healthcare to climate science to sustainable agriculture, and how meaningful research often starts with curiosity and collaboration. #IEEE #GHTC2025 #EthicalAI #MachineLearning #ComputerVision #Sustainability #Research

Someone making a simple tic tac toe game doesn't need Fable 5 At this point models at the bottom of the top 20 can easily do 87% of things as well as the models in the top 5 (at least for me) I was wondering why anyone would want to use Codex when we have Claude and Kimi I was pretty blown away when I looked into it If someone wanted a bang for a buck, they would go for Kimi (Moonshot AI) , and if they wanted frontier performance they would go to Anthropic OpenAI 's sandwiched in the middle, where it doesn't have the best value for money or models at the top of benchmarks I still bought the "plus" plan for $20 Why? Because the usage limits are BROKEN and Sol is INCREDIBLE 4 hour session with GPT Sol and Terra on 1.5x Speed (which uses significantly more tokens) only got me through 40% of my 5 hour usage, after which it reset On top of that, OpenAI regularly resets the weekly usage limits which gives even more compute! And even if you didn't get the exact output you wanted with your prompt in the first try, that's completely fine as it's all about iteration and prompting For example I was making a project for ByteByByte , and it took me 4 prompts to get it exactly how I needed it big announcements soon ;) At the end of the day, it's more about the creativity and idea, the model is just a tool What's one project you were building which caused your limits to finish?
